chapter: The Paradise and life in Queens
title: Musicians who visited the Paradise
summary: Billie Holiday, Bird, Ike Quebec, Hot Lips Page, Hawkins, Roy Eldridge, Red Allen and many others came by; it was like home.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Who were some of the people you were most friendly with, during this time? People that you really enjoyed seeing up there?

Well. Billie Holiday, she used to come in all the time and sit down and Bird, you know, we were friends. And he'd come in and play. I was always glad to see him. And, of course, Ike Quebec was there all the time and Hot Lips Page, I loved him so. And then Coleman would come by once in a while and Roy (Eldridge) and Red, Red Allen was there all the time and he and Lips used to get together and that was somethin', to hear them jammin', you know. And Budd Johnson used to come by, Joe Thomas, the tenor player, Wardell Gray, Sonny

Stitts (sic) and Gene Ammons and, you know, practically everybody, you know. There was so many. And Clark Terry and all those guys, you know. It was home. It was like home for the guys, you know. 'Cause I made 'em feel good when they came in there.
Did they serve food there at all?

Yeah, they had food, they had a kitchen, yeah. Just a small place. Yeah. A bar and tables and they had a little dance floor. But people remember me for that. And I thank God that I was able to do that.
